title: Reported Szijjártó–Lavrov call during Ukraine EU accession talks
description_short: A report on leaked recordings says Hungary’s foreign minister briefed Russia’s Lavrov during Ukraine accession talks on Dec. 14, 2023.
description_medium: A 2026 report by Telex on leaked-call material says Hungarian Foreign Minister Péter Szijjártó spoke with Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov on December 14, 2023, during European Council discussions on opening EU accession talks with Ukraine. The reported transcript has Lavrov ask about compromise language on minority rights and Szijjártó offer to send a related document through Hungary’s Moscow embassy. These reports do not establish a Trump connection or prove that the call blocked accession.
description_long: An April 2026 report by Telex, describing leaked call recordings published by an investigative consortium, quotes an exchange between Hungarian Foreign Minister Péter Szijjártó and Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov. VSquare dates the call to December 14, 2023, during a break at the European Council meeting in Brussels as leaders considered opening accession negotiations with Ukraine. In the transcript as reported, Lavrov asks about the compromise on opening talks and the role of minority-language provisions. Szijjártó says he can send a related document through Hungary’s embassy in Moscow for Lavrov’s chief of staff. Telex says the exact document was unclear and that Hungary’s foreign ministry did not answer the consortium’s questions. The reporting supports an attributed account of a call about the negotiations; it does not establish that the ministers successfully blocked Ukraine’s accession. The material inspected for this proposal does not independently authenticate the underlying recording or connect this December 2023 exchange to Donald Trump.
